## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

The refresh helper should preserve existing fingerprints: refreshing an edited tracked file currently replaces its baseline and causes verification to accept the edit.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — When `tracked.txt` has been edited since its fingerprint was recorded, passing `["tracked.txt", "new.txt"]` to `refresh_fingerprints` makes subsequent verification accept the edited file. The unconditional assignment overwrites the recorded digest; the refresh test passes because its tracked file remains unchanged. Preserve existing entries as `register_new_files` does, and add a regression test using an edited tracked file. — Refreshing after adding files can erase evidence of hand edits that the existing fingerprints are intended to detect.

## Strengths
- The registration test verifies that existing fingerprints survive hand edits and that verification still detects those edits.
